title: GPU-only params silently fabricate and then persist DEFAULT_PARAMS
description: When the incoming params contain only the GPU flag (params = { task_type: "GPU" }), displayParams is {} so effectiveParams falls back to DEFAULT_PARAMS. The textarea then shows iterations/learning_rate/depth/l2_leaf_reg/early_stopping_rounds that are NOT actually part of the saved config (misrepresentation of persisted state). Worse, because `draft` is seeded from those defaults, the next commit bakes them in: toggling the GPU checkbox off runs handleGpuToggle(false) -> current = JSON.parse(draft) = DEFAULT_PARAMS -> onUpdate("params", { ...DEFAULT_PARAMS }), silently writing 5 hyperparameters the user never chose. Likewise a blur commits { ...DEFAULT_PARAMS, task_type: "GPU" }. This state is reachable from any node/pipeline config authored outside this panel that sets params to just { task_type: GPU }.
evidence: L40 `const { task_type: _taskType, ...displayParams } = params` -> for params={task_type:'GPU'}, displayParams={}. L41 `effectiveParams = Object.keys(displayParams).length > 0 ? displayParams : DEFAULT_PARAMS` -> effectiveParams=DEFAULT_PARAMS. L42/46 draft and serialised = JSON.stringify(DEFAULT_PARAMS). L71 `current = JSON.parse(draft)` = DEFAULT_PARAMS. L72 disable branch `onUpdate('params', { ...current })` persists all 5 defaults. The DEFAULT_PARAMS fallback is meant for a genuinely empty config, but it also fires for GPU-only configs where the user has intentionally left hyperparameters unset.
